content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing a similar issue with [product_name] software version [version_no]. Today, I replaced my old [article_no] blocks with the new [version_no]. After updating the IP addresses for all modules and re-adding two slaves as new [version_no] devices, they appear correctly connected (see attached screenshot). All connections to the first block (master) work fine, but those to the two slaves do not trigger the network input. I simulated an online test by manually pressing the switch, but I'm unsure how to replicate a 'click' through the software. The 'Allow S7 access' option is enabled. I'm stuck on this and would appreciate any suggestions. Thank you!
Please upload your network project as a zip file to the forum for review.
I've attached the file here. Thank you!
I am unable to open your project in [product_name] [version_no]. An 'Unknown error' message appears when I try.
That's odd. I can open it on my Macbook using [product_name] version [version_no]. Maybe that's the cause? I'll try restarting the software to check again.
Possibly, but I'm not familiar with using MAC for this software.
I closed and reopened [product_name] [version_no], browsed my files, and opened the .SNP file. Is your file extension also SNP? Maybe I need to export it differently. I'll check that. Thanks!
When your network project is open, right-click the master device and export its program as a [product_name] file. Zip it and upload that file.
See attached file. Thanks!
Are you certain you added the [product_name] [version_no] slave devices to your network project?

Yes, I added the '[product_name] [version_no] Slave' and confirmed this in the attached screenshot. I transferred everything from the old [article_no] slaves to the new ones before deleting the old slaves.
The [product_name] file opens without any issue for me.
When you review the device properties, the 'Device type' is set to '[product_name] [version_no] Slave' for the Network Input. That seems correct.
I've rebuilt your network project using the [product_name] file you uploaded. Please give this a try. Did you set the actual devices 8_2 (192.168.1.102) and 8_3 (192.168.1.101) to slave mode?

I may have noticed something new. On the PLC display, in Diagnostics > Software > Data Connection: The master shows: 'S7 Client State: Disconnected' (Remote IP: 192.168.001.102, which is the second Slave). The two slaves show: 'Slave server State: Disconnected' (Remote IP: 000.000.000.000). Could this be a wiring issue?

Why are you using master/slave mode? Why not configure all three devices as masters? Using master/slave restricts the program resources of your two slaves, except for situations where they need to run independently during errors.

Previously, I had it set up the same way with my old [article_no] blocks and it worked. My reasoning was to have one master with the main configuration/diagram, and two slaves simply following the master, so only the master needed updates. We needed extra inputs and outputs, which was solved this way years ago, although I'm not certain it was optimal. Regarding your suggestion, would switching to a master/master setup mean each unit would have its own diagram? That might make things less visible at a glance and require splitting up the diagram. Thanks for your suggestion.

One more thing: Based on what you said, are the two slaves not working because the master reports a S7 Client Disconnected error? All lights connected to the master work, so I don't understand why this error shows. I toggled 'Allow S7 access' in offline settings and enabled 'Modbus access' just in case, as shown in the screenshot.

Exactly, in a master/master configuration, each device would have its own program. If the master fails in master/slave mode, the slaves also stop functioning. With individual programs, each device continues working even if there's an error on another. You only have S7 connections; Modbus doesn't need to be enabled.

Thanks for your input. I would prefer to fix the S7 issue first so that everything works as before. I'm not sure where the S7 problem is coming from or how to debug it. If the issue remains, I'll consider switching to master/master.

It's difficult to diagnose from afar, as I don't know the network layout or exactly what is being done. Are IP addresses possibly duplicated? Are the devices only directly connected, or are they part of a network with a router assigning IPs via DHCP?

It appears to be resolved. I set fixed IP addresses through the LCD display. Our home network uses DHCP, but the router selects unique IPs. To fix the issue, I stopped the program on the two slaves, changed their mode from Slave to Master, saved and restarted, then switched them back to Slave mode and restarted again. Everything now works and no error messages are present; all lights are functioning correctly for both master and slaves. The devices were always configured as slaves with the correct IPs and recognized by the software. It was a strange issue, but if anyone faces this in the future, this method might help. Thank you all for your assistance!

analysis.insight_summary: After upgrading from older hardware blocks to newer software and devices, users faced challenges with network input configuration—specifically, inputs connected to slave devices wouldn't trigger while master-related functions operated normally. File sharing for troubleshooting was further complicated by cross-platform compatibility issues and project export methods.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect network inputs to work reliably and project files to be compatible across platforms and software versions. They also desire clear processes for device setup and troubleshooting to resolve such issues efficiently.
